intro: At B1 you summarised short texts for someone else, and at B2 you described graphs in writing. Now you put both to work for real people: explain a table of figures to someone who can't see it, summarise a long article (in Indonesian or English) for your manager, a foreign colleague or a client, and keep a project group working together towards its goal.
teachingNotes: Build on the chain and recap each in a line, don't re-teach: b2-describing-data (trend words rise / fall / peak, to vs by, twice as high as, slightly lower than, about / just over / nearly, a quarter / a third / half; an overview with the main trends and no numbers; no reasons or opinions), b2-reading-strategies (skim for the gist, scan for one fact, the writer's attitude, reading a long report through its summary and conclusion), b1-mediation-summaries (main point first + 2–3 key facts, in your own words, accurate, nothing added, no opinion; The email says …) and a2-mediation-messages (passing on the key facts of a notice). Strand ME: mediation = helping other people understand something or work together. New here: SPEAKING about data to a listener, choosing what to keep for a particular reader, and facilitating a group. Contexts: a survey table, a long Indonesian or English article, a university project group. Every table and article in this lesson is invented practice material: never present the figures as real statistics or the articles as real news, and don't attribute them to BPS or to a real newspaper.

Explaining data orally (to someone on the phone or a video call, or a manager who isn't a numbers person): the listener can't see the table and can't remember ten numbers. Order: 1) what the table is about (This table shows how / where / how many …), 2) the big picture first, like the overview in a written report (Basically, … / The main thing to notice is …), 3) only 2–3 key numbers, rounded, 4) check understanding (Does that make sense? / Any questions so far?). Rounding: 48.7% → just under half; 51.2% → just over half; 32.4% → about a third / roughly one in three; 24.6% → nearly a quarter / about one in four; 66% → about two thirds; 9.8% → about one in ten; 2,040,000 → just over two million. Common errors: reading every figure in table order; starting with a detail; Indonesian decimals: 48,7% is written 48.7% in English and said 'forty-eight point seven per cent' (never 'comma'), and Indonesian 2.040.000 = English 2,040,000; 'one from five' (from 'satu dari lima') → one in five; per cent (British) / percent (American) are both fine. 'One in five workers go / goes' are both used: accept both. Speaking is not an IELTS report: short sentences, rounded numbers, 'you', and a check at the end. If the listener asks why, a reason is fine, but say it as a guess (It might be because …), separate from the facts.

Summarising a long article for a specific audience. Ask first: who is it for, and what will they do with it? The same article gives different summaries: a MANAGER wants the decision points (what we need to decide, the options, the cost, the deadline): The decision we need to make is whether … or … / We need to decide by …; a FOREIGN COLLEAGUE needs context, the background an Indonesian already knows (what an institution, rule or term is, why it matters here): For context, … / In Indonesia, …; a CLIENT wants the impact on them (what changes for them, when, what they have to do): For you, this means … / The main change for you is …. Process: skim for the gist, scan for the facts THIS reader needs, then write from notes, not sentence by sentence; from an Indonesian article don't translate word for word (pukul 22.00 → 10 p.m.; keep names, explain terms: ganjil-genap = the odd-even number plate rule). Keep it short: the main point for that reader first, then 2–3 points. Keep the facts, the writer's opinion (The writer argues that …) and your own suggestion (My suggestion would be …, a phrase to remember) clearly apart. Common errors: following the article's order (background first), the same summary for everyone, putting everything in, internal problems (costs, staff) in a client summary, word-for-word translation, adding an opinion as if it were in the article.

Facilitating group work: the facilitator (fasilitator, the person who leads the discussion) helps the group do the task; they don't do it alone. Five moves: opening the task (Our aim today is to … / By the end of this session, we need to … / Let's start with …); inviting views (Sari, what's your take? / Dimas, we haven't heard from you yet. / What do the rest of you think? / Does anyone see it differently?); keeping on track (That's an interesting point, but let's come back to it later. / Let's get back to … / I think we're getting a bit off track.); time-keeping (We've got five minutes left. / We're running out of time, so … / Let's spend ten minutes on each part.); summarising agreement and next steps (So, we've agreed to / that … / So, to sum up, … / Rina is going to … by Friday. / Let's meet again on …). Indonesian traps: 'Let's back to the topic' (Ayo kembali ke topik: back is not a verb) → Let's get back / go back to the topic; 'We have five minutes again' (lima menit lagi) → We've got five minutes left / five more minutes; take in 'What's your take?' = your view (pandangan), not 'ambil'; 'Any opinion?' sounds abrupt → Any thoughts? / What do you all think?. Culture: in many Indonesian groups the quiet members wait to be asked and the ketua kelompok ends up doing the work; inviting someone by name is kind, not rude. Thank the person who talked a lot before moving on (Thanks, Dimas. Let's hear from someone else.), and never call someone out ('Why are you so quiet?').

Limits: A0–B1 grammar plus the chain. No third conditional, wish, past modals, participle clauses or non-defining relative clauses; 'What this means for you is …' and 'My suggestion would be …' are phrases to remember. Don't teach chairing a formal meeting, writing minutes, negotiating or presentation structure (b2-presentations). When the learner practises, play the listener, the reader or a group member: react to the content, then correct ONE thing (usually reading every figure, background first for a manager, 'one from five', 'Let's back to' or 'five minutes again'). Grading: any short natural answer with the key facts or the right move is right; understandable but unnatural English gets partial credit; an answer in Indonesian shows understanding but asks for English. Test only clear cases.

keyPoints.title: Explaining data aloud: big picture, few numbers, rounded
keyPoints.explanation: Your listener can't see the table and can't remember ten numbers. Say what the table is about, give the big picture first (Basically, …), then only two or three key numbers, rounded (just under half, about a third, one in ten), and check understanding (Does that make sense?). Don't read every figure. English writes 48.7% and says 'forty-eight point seven per cent', never 'comma'.

examples.en: Basically, most people still buy their groceries at a market or a minimarket.
examples.id: Intinya, kebanyakan orang masih membeli belanjaan dapur di pasar atau minimarket.

examples.en: Just under half of the students live in a kos.
examples.id: Hampir separuh mahasiswa tinggal di kos.

examples.en: Does that make sense so far?
examples.id: Sejauh ini masuk akal, kan? / Sudah jelas sejauh ini?

id.title: Menjelaskan data secara lisan: gambaran besar, sedikit angka, dibulatkan
id.explanation: Pendengarmu tidak bisa melihat tabelnya dan tidak bisa mengingat sepuluh angka. Katakan tabel itu tentang apa, berikan gambaran besarnya dulu (Basically, …), lalu hanya dua atau tiga angka penting yang dibulatkan (just under half, about a third, one in ten), dan cek pemahamannya (Does that make sense?). Jangan bacakan semua angka. Bahasa Inggris menulis 48.7% dan membacanya 'forty-eight point seven per cent', tidak pernah 'comma'.

keyPoints.title: Summarising for a specific reader: keep what THEY need
keyPoints.explanation: Ask first: who is it for, and what do they need? A manager wants the decision points (options, cost, deadline); a foreign colleague needs context (what an Indonesian already knows); a client wants the impact on them (what changes, when, what to do). Put the main point for that reader first, add two or three points, and leave the rest out. Write from notes, not sentence by sentence, and keep the facts, the writer's opinion and your own suggestion apart.

examples.en: The decision we need to make is whether to sign the new contract or look for another office.
examples.id: Keputusan yang perlu kita ambil adalah apakah menandatangani kontrak baru atau mencari kantor lain.

examples.en: For context, Jakarta's air is often very bad in the dry season.
examples.id: Sebagai konteks, udara Jakarta sering sangat buruk di musim kemarau.

examples.en: For you, this means your orders will arrive a day later next week.
examples.id: Buat Anda, artinya pesanan Anda akan tiba sehari lebih lambat minggu depan.

id.title: Meringkas untuk pembaca tertentu: simpan apa yang MEREKA butuhkan
id.explanation: Tanya dulu: ringkasan ini untuk siapa, dan apa yang mereka butuhkan? Manajer ingin poin keputusannya (pilihan, biaya, tenggat); rekan kerja asing butuh konteks (hal yang orang Indonesia sudah tahu); klien ingin tahu dampaknya bagi mereka (apa yang berubah, kapan, apa yang harus dilakukan). Taruh poin utama untuk pembaca itu di depan, tambahkan dua atau tiga poin, dan buang sisanya. Tulis dari catatan, bukan kalimat per kalimat, dan pisahkan fakta, opini penulis dan saranmu sendiri.

keyPoints.title: Facilitating group work: open, invite, steer, keep time, sum up
keyPoints.explanation: A facilitator helps the group do the task. Open the task (Our aim today is to …), invite views by name (Sari, what's your take? / Dimas, we haven't heard from you yet.), keep the group on track (That's an interesting point, but let's come back to it later.), keep time (We've got ten minutes left.) and sum up what you agreed and who does what next (So, we've agreed to … Rina is going to …).

examples.en: Our aim today is to choose the questions for our survey.
examples.id: Tujuan kita hari ini adalah memilih pertanyaan untuk survei kita.

examples.en: So, to sum up, Budi is going to book the room by Friday.
examples.id: Jadi, kesimpulannya, Budi akan memesan ruangannya paling lambat Jumat.

id.title: Memfasilitasi kerja kelompok: membuka, mengajak, mengarahkan, menjaga waktu, menyimpulkan
id.explanation: Fasilitator membantu kelompok menyelesaikan tugasnya. Buka tugasnya (Our aim today is to …), ajak orang berpendapat dengan menyebut namanya (Sari, what's your take? / Dimas, we haven't heard from you yet.), jaga agar diskusi tetap terarah (That's an interesting point, but let's come back to it later.), jaga waktu (We've got ten minutes left.) dan simpulkan apa yang sudah disepakati serta siapa melakukan apa berikutnya (So, we've agreed to … Rina is going to …).

36.5% thirty-six point five percent

guidedPractice.hint: English uses a point, not a comma, for decimals, and you say 'point'.

expected: the decision she needs to make
the decision

let's go back to the topic

expected: aim

independentPractice.prompt: A friend can't see this table. Explain it in two or three short sentences: where 300 students at a campus in Yogyakarta live (practice figures): with parents 52.3% · in a kos 38.0% · other 9.7%.
expected: basically most students live with their parents or in a kos just over half live with their parents and nearly four in ten live in a kos only about one in ten live somewhere else
most students live with their parents or in a kos just over half live with their parents and about four in ten live in a kos does that make sense
independentPractice.hint: Big picture first (Basically, …), then two rounded numbers (just over half, nearly four in ten), then a check (Does that make sense?).

independentPractice.prompt: A practice news article says the toll road between Jakarta and Bandung will be closed at night next week for repairs, so trucks will take a longer road. Your client in Bandung gets parcels from you every day. Write one sentence for her.
expected: for you this means your parcels may arrive a day late next week
for you this means some parcels may arrive later than usual next week
next week your parcels might arrive a bit later because of road repairs
independentPractice.hint: A client wants the impact on them: For you, this means …

expected: so we've agreed to do online shopping habits dimas is going to make the slides by wednesday
so to sum up our topic is online shopping habits dimas is going to make the slides by wednesday
so we've agreed that our topic is online shopping habits dimas will make the slides by wednesday
independentPractice.hint: So, we've agreed to / that … + who is going to do what, and by when.

assessment.prompt: A survey of 2,000 office workers in Surabaya (practice figures, not real statistics) shows how they get to work: motorbike 48.7% · car 21.4% · bus or train 19.6% · bicycle or walking 10.3%. You're explaining it to your manager on the phone. Complete with a rounded amount: About one in ___ workers go by bus or train.
assessment.rubric: Correct: five (19.6% is about 20%: one in five = one person out of every five). 'four' = 0 (one in four = 25%). 'three' = 0 (about 33%). 'ten' = 0 (10%). 'twenty' = 10 (that's the percentage, not 'one in …'). 'from five' = 30 (copies 'satu dari lima': the sentence already has 'in').

assessment.prompt: You're explaining a survey about phone use (practice figures) to a new colleague on a video call. Put the three parts in the best order and write the letters. A: Does that make sense so far? B: Just over a third use their phone mainly for work, and roughly one in ten hardly use it at all. C: Basically, most people in the survey spend more than five hours a day on their phone.
assessment.rubric: Correct: C B A (C = the big picture first, B = two or three rounded key numbers, A = check understanding at the end). 'B C A' = 40 (details before the big picture: the listener doesn't know what the numbers are about). 'A' first or in the middle = 20. Any order that starts with C but puts A before B = 50.

assessment.prompt: Mark, a new colleague from Australia who doesn't read Indonesian, sees this practice article: 'Mulai 1 Maret, truk barang beroda lebih dari empat dilarang melintas di jalan-jalan utama Jakarta Pusat pukul 06.00–22.00. Aturan ini sudah diuji coba selama enam bulan di tiga ruas jalan.' Complete his summary in English: From 1 March, big trucks can't use the main roads in central Jakarta between 6 in the morning and ___.
assessment.rubric: Correct: 10 at night / 10 p.m. (pukul 22.00 = 10 p.m.: subtract 12 from a 24-hour time after noon). '10 in the evening' = 100. '22.00' or '22:00' = 100 (the 24-hour clock is clear in writing). '22' alone = 60 (unclear in English speech). '10' alone = 50 (could be 10 in the morning). '12 at night', '2 p.m.', '8 p.m.' or any other time = 0. A translation of the whole article = 50 if the time is right (too long: Mark asked what it's about).

assessment.prompt: A long practice article explains a new rule for delivery trucks in central Jakarta. Your notes: A: The city tested the rule on three roads for six months. B: Traffic jams on those roads fell by about a fifth. C: Orders to central Jakarta that come in after 4 p.m. will usually arrive the next morning. D: Our company has to choose between night shifts and smaller vans. Bu Rina runs an online batik shop in Bekasi and sends her parcels with your company. Which note should your summary for her start with? Write the letter.
assessment.rubric: Correct: C (a client wants the impact on them: what changes for her customers' orders). D = 20 (that's the decision point for your manager; a client doesn't need your internal problems). A or B = 10 (background and context, useful for a foreign colleague, not the first thing a client needs).

assessment.prompt: You're leading a project group at a university in Bandung. For ten minutes everyone has been talking about a K-drama. Complete what you say to bring them back to the task (two words): That's fun, but we're getting a bit off track. Let's ___ to the survey questions.
assessment.rubric: Correct: get back (Let's get back to …). 'go back' and 'come back' = 100. 'return' = 100 (one word, but natural: Let's return to …). 'back' alone = 20 (the Indonesian 'Ayo kembali ke …': back isn't a verb, so 'Let's back to' is wrong). 'stop talking' or anything rude = 0 for the move.

assessment.prompt: In the same group, Dimas has done most of the talking and Rina hasn't spoken for twenty minutes. Complete the polite invitation (three words): Thanks, Dimas. Rina, we haven't ___ yet.
assessment.rubric: Correct: heard from you (We haven't heard from you yet: a kind way to invite a quiet person by name). 'heard your view / opinion / thoughts / ideas / take' = 100. 'listened to you' = 70 (understood, but 'heard from you' is the fixed phrase). 'heard you' = 60 (sounds like we couldn't hear her voice). Any answer that blames her ('Why are you so quiet?') = 0.

assessment.prompt: It's the end of the session. Your notes: agreed → an online survey, not interviews · Rina → writes the questions → by Friday. Write the missing word: So, to ___ up, we've agreed to do an online survey, and Rina is going to write the questions by Friday.
assessment.rubric: Correct: sum (So, to sum up, … : the fixed phrase that starts a summary of what the group agreed and who does what next). 'summarise' or 'summarize' = 30 ('to summarise' is right without 'up', but 'to summarise up' is wrong). 'wrap' = 60 ('to wrap up' is used to end a meeting, not to start a summary). 'conclude' = 20 ('to conclude up' is wrong). 'make' or 'end' = 0.

material.title: Explaining a table to someone who can't see it

blocks.text:
In b2-describing-data you **wrote** about charts. Now you **say** it: on the phone, on a video call, or to a manager who isn't a numbers person. Your listener can't see the table and can't remember ten numbers, so you choose for them. Use the same order every time:
1. **What it's about:** *This table shows where people buy their groceries.*
2. **The big picture first**, like the overview in a written report: *Basically, …* / *The main thing to notice is …*
3. **Two or three key numbers, rounded**: *just under half, about a third, one in ten* (next section).
4. **Check understanding:** *Does that make sense?* / *Any questions so far?*

Don't read every figure in table order: after the third number, nobody is listening.

id.text:
Di b2-describing-data kamu **menulis** tentang grafik. Sekarang kamu **mengucapkannya**: di telepon, di video call, atau kepada manajer yang tidak terlalu paham angka. Pendengarmu tidak bisa melihat tabelnya dan tidak bisa mengingat sepuluh angka, jadi kamu yang memilihkan untuk mereka. Pakai urutan yang sama setiap kali:
1. **Tentang apa:** *This table shows where people buy their groceries.*
2. **Gambaran besar dulu**, seperti overview di laporan tertulis: *Basically, …* / *The main thing to notice is …*
3. **Dua atau tiga angka penting, dibulatkan**: *just under half, about a third, one in ten* (bagian berikutnya).
4. **Cek pemahaman:** *Does that make sense?* / *Any questions so far?*

Jangan bacakan semua angka sesuai urutan tabel: setelah angka ketiga, tidak ada yang mendengarkan lagi.

blocks.text: Example table: Where households in a city buy most of their groceries (practice figures, not real statistics): traditional market 41.8% · minimarket 33.1% · supermarket 15.4% · online 9.7%. Here is how Rina explains it to her manager, Pak Hasan, on the phone:

id.text: Contoh tabel: Tempat rumah tangga di sebuah kota membeli sebagian besar belanjaan dapurnya (angka latihan, bukan statistik asli): traditional market 41.8% · minimarket 33.1% · supermarket 15.4% · online 9.7%. Begini cara Rina menjelaskannya kepada manajernya, Pak Hasan, lewat telepon:

rows.en: This table shows where families in the city buy most of their groceries.
rows.id: Tabel ini menunjukkan di mana keluarga di kota itu membeli sebagian besar belanjaan dapurnya.

rows.en: Basically, most people still shop in person, not online.
rows.id: Intinya, kebanyakan orang masih belanja langsung, bukan online.

rows.en: The traditional market is the most popular: just over four in ten families shop there.
rows.id: Pasar tradisional paling populer: sedikit lebih dari empat dari sepuluh keluarga belanja di sana.
rows.note: 3 · key number: 41.8% → just over four in ten

id.note: 3 · angka penting: 41.8% → just over four in ten

rows.en: About a third use a minimarket, and only about one in ten shop online.
rows.id: Sekitar sepertiga belanja di minimarket, dan hanya sekitar satu dari sepuluh yang belanja online.
rows.note: 3 · 33.1% → about a third · 9.7% → about one in ten

id.note: 3 · 33.1% → about a third · 9.7% → about one in ten

rows.en: Does that make sense so far?
rows.id: Sejauh ini sudah jelas?

blocks.text: Speaking is not an IELTS report. Use short sentences, round the numbers, talk to the listener (*you*), and stop to check. Rina skipped the supermarket figure completely: that's fine, it wasn't one of the key points. If Pak Hasan asks why, she can guess, but she says it's a guess: *It might be because markets are cheaper.*

id.text: Berbicara itu bukan laporan IELTS. Pakai kalimat pendek, bulatkan angkanya, bicara langsung ke pendengar (*you*), dan berhenti untuk mengecek. Rina sama sekali tidak menyebut angka supermarket: tidak apa-apa, itu bukan poin penting. Kalau Pak Hasan bertanya kenapa, Rina boleh menebak, tapi ia bilang bahwa itu tebakan: *It might be because markets are cheaper.*

blocks.prompt: Budi has to explain a survey table to his manager on the phone. What should he say first?
options: Every figure in the table, row by row.
The big picture, for example: Basically, most people still shop in person.
blocks.explain: Start with **the big picture**, so the listener knows what the numbers are about. Reading every row loses the listener, and reasons are guesses that come later, if he's asked.

id.prompt: Budi harus menjelaskan tabel survei kepada manajernya lewat telepon. Apa yang sebaiknya ia katakan pertama kali?
id.explain: Mulailah dengan **gambaran besarnya**, supaya pendengar tahu angka-angka itu tentang apa. Membacakan setiap baris membuat pendengar bingung, dan alasan hanyalah tebakan yang datang belakangan, kalau ia ditanya.

id.title: Menjelaskan tabel kepada orang yang tidak bisa melihatnya

material.title: Rounding numbers so people remember them

blocks.text:
A listener remembers **just under half** much better than **48.7 per cent**. You already know *about, nearly, just over* and *a quarter, a third, half* from b2-describing-data. Two more tools for speaking:
- **just under / just over**: a little less / a little more than a round number.
- **one in + number**: *one in three* (about 33%), *one in four* (25%), *one in ten* (10%). It means *one person out of every three / four / ten*.

Round only when the exact figure doesn't matter. If your manager needs the exact number for a report, give it, and say it the English way.

id.text:
Pendengar jauh lebih mudah mengingat **just under half** daripada **48.7 per cent**. Kamu sudah tahu *about, nearly, just over* dan *a quarter, a third, half* dari b2-describing-data. Dua alat lagi untuk berbicara:
- **just under / just over**: sedikit kurang / sedikit lebih dari angka bulat.
- **one in + angka**: *one in three* (sekitar 33%), *one in four* (25%), *one in ten* (10%). Artinya *satu orang dari setiap tiga / empat / sepuluh orang*.

Bulatkan hanya kalau angka tepatnya tidak penting. Kalau manajermu butuh angka persisnya untuk laporan, berikan angkanya, dan ucapkan dengan cara bahasa Inggris.

rows.en: 48.7% → just under half
rows.id: 48,7% → hampir separuh

rows.en: 51.2% → just over half
rows.id: 51,2% → sedikit lebih dari separuh

rows.en: 32.4% → about a third / roughly one in three
rows.id: 32,4% → sekitar sepertiga / kira-kira satu dari tiga

rows.en: 24.6% → nearly a quarter / about one in four
rows.id: 24,6% → hampir seperempat / sekitar satu dari empat

rows.en: 66% → about two thirds
rows.id: 66% → sekitar dua pertiga

rows.en: 2,040,000 → just over two million
rows.id: 2.040.000 → sedikit lebih dari dua juta

id.note: bahasa Inggris memakai koma untuk ribuan

blocks.text:
Indonesian traps:
- **Decimals:** Indonesian 48,7% = English **48.7%**, said *forty-eight **point** seven per cent*, never `forty-eight comma seven`. And Indonesian 2.040.000 = English **2,040,000**.
- ***satu dari lima*** = **one in five**, not `one from five`.
- *per cent* (British) and *percent* (American) are both fine.
- *One in ten people **use** / **uses** it* are both heard: don't worry about it.

id.text:
Jebakan bahasa Indonesia:
- **Desimal:** 48,7% dalam bahasa Indonesia = **48.7%** dalam bahasa Inggris, dibaca *forty-eight **point** seven per cent*, tidak pernah `forty-eight comma seven`. Dan 2.040.000 = **2,040,000** dalam bahasa Inggris.
- ***satu dari lima*** = **one in five**, bukan `one from five`.
- *per cent* (British) dan *percent* (Amerika) sama-sama benar.
- *One in ten people **use** / **uses** it* dua-duanya sering dipakai: tidak usah khawatir.

blocks.prompt: A survey (practice figures) says 33.8% of the staff cycle to work. How do you say it on a call?
blocks.explain: 33.8% is close to 33%: that's **a third**. *A quarter* is 25%, and *one from three* copies *satu dari tiga*: English says *one in three*.

id.prompt: Sebuah survei (angka latihan) mengatakan 33,8% karyawan bersepeda ke kantor. Bagaimana kamu mengucapkannya di telepon?
id.explain: 33,8% dekat dengan 33%, yaitu **a third** (sepertiga). *A quarter* itu 25%, dan *one from three* meniru *satu dari tiga*: bahasa Inggris bilang *one in three*.

blocks.text:
Quick recap from B1: a good summary gives **the main point first**, then the **2–3 key facts**, in your own words, with nothing added. At B2 the articles are long, so you have to **choose**. Before you write, ask: **Who is it for, and what will they do with it?**
- **Your manager** wants the **decision points**: what we need to decide, the options, the cost, the deadline. *The decision we need to make is whether … or …*
- **A foreign colleague** needs **context**: what every Indonesian already knows but they don't. *For context, …* / *In Indonesia, …*
- **A client** wants the **impact on them**: what changes for them, when, and what they have to do. *For you, this means …*

How: skim for the gist, scan for the facts THIS reader needs, close the article and write from your notes. With an Indonesian article, don't translate sentence by sentence: tell the reader what matters to them.

id.text:
Ulasan singkat dari B1: ringkasan yang baik memberi **poin utama dulu**, lalu **2–3 fakta penting**, dengan kata-katamu sendiri, tanpa tambahan. Di B2 artikelnya panjang, jadi kamu harus **memilih**. Sebelum menulis, tanya: **Untuk siapa, dan akan dipakai untuk apa?**
- **Manajermu** ingin **poin keputusannya**: apa yang perlu kita putuskan, pilihan-pilihannya, biayanya, tenggatnya. *The decision we need to make is whether … or …*
- **Rekan kerja asing** butuh **konteks**: hal yang semua orang Indonesia sudah tahu tapi mereka belum. *For context, …* / *In Indonesia, …*
- **Klien** ingin tahu **dampaknya bagi mereka**: apa yang berubah untuk mereka, kapan, dan apa yang harus mereka lakukan. *For you, this means …*

Caranya: skim untuk menangkap intinya, scan untuk fakta yang dibutuhkan pembaca INI, tutup artikelnya lalu tulis dari catatanmu. Kalau artikelnya berbahasa Indonesia, jangan terjemahkan kalimat per kalimat: sampaikan apa yang penting bagi pembacanya.

blocks.text: A practice article (the content is invented): 'MULAI JUNI, KANTOR DI JAKARTA WAJIB WFH DUA HARI SEMINGGU. Pemerintah provinsi mewajibkan perusahaan swasta di Jakarta menerapkan kerja dari rumah setiap Selasa dan Kamis selama musim kemarau, Juni sampai September. Tujuannya mengurangi kemacetan dan polusi udara, yang biasanya paling buruk pada bulan-bulan itu. Perusahaan yang melanggar bisa didenda. Layanan pelanggan, rumah sakit dan toko tetap buka seperti biasa.' Three summaries of the same article:

id.text: Artikel latihan (isinya karangan): 'MULAI JUNI, KANTOR DI JAKARTA WAJIB WFH DUA HARI SEMINGGU. Pemerintah provinsi mewajibkan perusahaan swasta di Jakarta menerapkan kerja dari rumah setiap Selasa dan Kamis selama musim kemarau, Juni sampai September. Tujuannya mengurangi kemacetan dan polusi udara, yang biasanya paling buruk pada bulan-bulan itu. Perusahaan yang melanggar bisa didenda. Layanan pelanggan, rumah sakit dan toko tetap buka seperti biasa.' Tiga ringkasan dari artikel yang sama:

rows.en: From June to September, we have to work from home on Tuesdays and Thursdays. We need to decide which meetings move online, and whether five more people need laptops.
rows.id: Dari Juni sampai September, kita harus bekerja dari rumah setiap Selasa dan Kamis. Kita perlu memutuskan rapat mana yang pindah ke online, dan apakah lima orang lagi butuh laptop.
rows.note: for the manager: the decision points

rows.en: For context, Jakarta's air is often very bad in the dry season, from about June to September, and traffic is a big part of the problem. So the city is making companies work from home two days a week.
rows.id: Sebagai konteks, udara Jakarta sering sangat buruk di musim kemarau, kira-kira Juni sampai September, dan lalu lintas adalah penyebab besarnya. Jadi pemerintah kota mewajibkan perusahaan bekerja dari rumah dua hari seminggu.
rows.note: for a foreign colleague: the context

rows.en: For you, nothing changes with your orders: our customer service is open as normal. But from June to September, our meetings with you on Tuesdays and Thursdays will be online.
rows.id: Buat Anda, tidak ada yang berubah dengan pesanan Anda: layanan pelanggan kami tetap buka seperti biasa. Tapi dari Juni sampai September, rapat kami dengan Anda setiap Selasa dan Kamis akan diadakan online.
rows.note: for a client: the impact on them

blocks.text: Common mistakes: following the article's order (background first, while your manager is waiting for the decision); one summary for everyone; putting everything in; telling a client about your internal problems (costs, staff, laptops). And keep three things apart: the **facts** (*The article says …*), the **writer's opinion** (*The writer argues that …*) and **your own suggestion** (*My suggestion would be …*, a phrase to remember).

id.text: Kesalahan yang sering terjadi: mengikuti urutan artikel (latar belakang dulu, padahal manajermu menunggu keputusannya); satu ringkasan untuk semua orang; memasukkan semuanya; menceritakan masalah internal (biaya, karyawan, laptop) kepada klien. Dan pisahkan tiga hal: **fakta** (*The article says …*), **opini penulis** (*The writer argues that …*) dan **saranmu sendiri** (*My suggestion would be …*, frasa untuk dihafal).

blocks.prompt: Mark, who has just moved to Jakarta from Australia, asks why everyone is talking about the new work-from-home rule. Which sentence helps him most?
options: We need to decide whether five more people need laptops.
For context, Jakarta's air is often very bad in the dry season, and traffic is a big part of the problem.
Our customer service is open as normal.
blocks.explain: Mark is a **foreign colleague**: he needs **context**, the background every Indonesian already knows. The laptops are a decision for the manager, and the customer service line is for a client.

id.prompt: Mark, yang baru pindah ke Jakarta dari Australia, bertanya kenapa semua orang membicarakan aturan kerja dari rumah yang baru. Kalimat mana yang paling membantunya?
id.explain: Mark adalah **rekan kerja asing**: ia butuh **konteks**, latar belakang yang semua orang Indonesia sudah tahu. Soal laptop adalah keputusan untuk manajer, dan kalimat layanan pelanggan untuk klien.

blocks.text:
A **facilitator** (fasilitator: the person who leads the discussion) helps the group do the task. They don't do it all themselves. Picture a project group at a university in Bandung: Sari, Dimas, Rina and Lukas, an exchange student from Germany. Their task: plan a survey for a class project. The facilitator has five moves:
1. **Open the task:** *Our aim today is to … / By the end of this session, we need to …*
2. **Invite views:** *Sari, what's your take? / Dimas, we haven't heard from you yet. / What do the rest of you think?*
3. **Keep on track:** *That's an interesting point, but let's come back to it later. / I think we're getting a bit off track.*
4. **Keep time:** *We've got ten minutes left. / We're running out of time, so …*
5. **Sum up and agree next steps:** *So, to sum up, … / So, we've agreed to … / Rina is going to … by Friday.*

id.text:
**Fasilitator** (orang yang memimpin diskusi) membantu kelompok menyelesaikan tugasnya. Ia tidak mengerjakan semuanya sendiri. Bayangkan sebuah kelompok proyek di sebuah universitas di Bandung: Sari, Dimas, Rina dan Lukas, mahasiswa pertukaran dari Jerman. Tugas mereka: merencanakan survei untuk proyek kuliah. Fasilitator punya lima langkah:
1. **Membuka tugas:** *Our aim today is to … / By the end of this session, we need to …*
2. **Mengajak berpendapat:** *Sari, what's your take? / Dimas, we haven't heard from you yet. / What do the rest of you think?*
3. **Menjaga agar tetap terarah:** *That's an interesting point, but let's come back to it later. / I think we're getting a bit off track.*
4. **Menjaga waktu:** *We've got ten minutes left. / We're running out of time, so …*
5. **Menyimpulkan dan menyepakati langkah berikutnya:** *So, to sum up, … / So, we've agreed to … / Rina is going to … by Friday.*

rows.en: By the end of this session, we need to agree on ten survey questions.
rows.id: Di akhir sesi ini, kita perlu menyepakati sepuluh pertanyaan survei.
rows.note: open the task: say the goal

rows.en: Lukas, what do you think? Is it the same in Germany?
rows.id: Lukas, bagaimana menurutmu? Apakah di Jerman sama?

rows.en: Thanks, Sari. Let's hear from someone else.
rows.id: Terima kasih, Sari. Ayo kita dengar dari yang lain.
rows.note: after someone has talked a lot

rows.en: That's an interesting point, but let's come back to it later.
rows.id: Itu poin yang menarik, tapi kita bahas lagi nanti, ya.

rows.en: We're running out of time, so let's choose the last two questions now.
rows.id: Waktu kita hampir habis, jadi ayo pilih dua pertanyaan terakhir sekarang.

rows.en: So, we've agreed to send the survey on Monday. Lukas is going to check the English.
rows.id: Jadi, kita sudah sepakat mengirim survei hari Senin. Lukas akan mengecek bahasa Inggrisnya.
rows.note: sum up: what we agreed + who does what

id.note: menyimpulkan: apa yang disepakati + siapa melakukan apa

blocks.text:
Indonesian traps:
- ***Ayo kembali ke topik*** → **Let's get back to the topic** (or *go back*), not `Let's back to the topic`: *back* isn't a verb here.
- ***Lima menit lagi*** → **We've got five minutes left** (or *five more minutes*), not `We have five minutes again`: here *lagi* means *left*.
- In *What's your take?*, **take** means *your view* (pandanganmu), not *ambil*.
- *Any opinion?* sounds abrupt: say *Any thoughts?* or *What do you all think?*
Culture: in many Indonesian groups the quiet members wait to be asked, and the ketua kelompok ends up doing all the work. Inviting someone by name is kind, not rude. But never put them on the spot: not `Why are you so quiet?`

id.text:
Jebakan bahasa Indonesia:
- ***Ayo kembali ke topik*** → **Let's get back to the topic** (atau *go back*), bukan `Let's back to the topic`: *back* di sini bukan kata kerja.
- ***Lima menit lagi*** → **We've got five minutes left** (atau *five more minutes*), bukan `We have five minutes again`: di sini *lagi* berarti *tersisa* (left).
- Dalam *What's your take?*, **take** berarti *pandanganmu*, bukan *ambil*.
- *Any opinion?* terdengar kaku: katakan *Any thoughts?* atau *What do you all think?*
Budaya: di banyak kelompok di Indonesia, anggota yang pendiam menunggu ditanya, dan akhirnya ketua kelompok yang mengerjakan semuanya. Mengajak seseorang dengan menyebut namanya itu baik, bukan kasar. Tapi jangan memojokkan: jangan bilang `Why are you so quiet?`

blocks.prompt: It's 3.50, and the session ends at 4.00. What does the facilitator say?
blocks.explain: **left** = *tersisa*: *We've got ten minutes left*. *again* copies *lagi*, but in English *again* means *one more time*. *We are late* means the session started late: that isn't the point.

id.prompt: Sekarang pukul 3.50, dan sesinya selesai pukul 4.00. Apa yang dikatakan fasilitator?
id.explain: **left** = *tersisa*: *We've got ten minutes left*. *again* meniru *lagi*, padahal dalam bahasa Inggris *again* berarti *sekali lagi*. *We are late* berarti sesinya terlambat, bukan itu maksudnya.

suggestedQuestions: How many numbers should I give when I explain a table on the phone?
How do I say 48,7% in English?
What's the difference between a summary for my manager and one for a client?
How can I invite a quiet person in my group without embarrassing them?

resources.title: Creating a study group (B2 listening)
resources.note: Listen to three students plan a study group: they choose a place, agree on a time and find a compromise, with useful phrases like What do you think?, Is that OK with you? and So everyone agrees…? It's about agreeing as a group, not about leading one, and has exercises and a worksheet.

id.note: Dengarkan tiga mahasiswa merencanakan kelompok belajar: mereka memilih tempat, menyepakati waktu dan mencari jalan tengah, dengan frasa berguna seperti What do you think?, Is that OK with you? dan So everyone agrees…? Fokusnya pada bersepakat sebagai kelompok, bukan memimpin kelompok, dan ada latihan serta lembar kerjanya.

id.intro: Di B1 kamu meringkas teks pendek untuk orang lain, dan di B2 kamu mendeskripsikan grafik secara tertulis. Sekarang kamu memakai keduanya untuk orang sungguhan: menjelaskan tabel angka kepada orang yang tidak bisa melihatnya, meringkas artikel panjang (bahasa Indonesia atau Inggris) untuk manajermu, rekan kerja asing atau klien, dan menjaga kelompok proyek tetap bekerja sama menuju tujuannya.
suggestedQuestions: Berapa banyak angka yang sebaiknya kusebut saat menjelaskan tabel lewat telepon?
Bagaimana cara mengucapkan 48,7% dalam bahasa Inggris?
Apa bedanya ringkasan untuk manajerku dan ringkasan untuk klien?
Bagaimana cara mengajak orang yang pendiam di kelompokku tanpa membuatnya malu?

assessment.mdt-1: Survei terhadap 2.000 pekerja kantor di Surabaya (angka latihan, bukan statistik asli) menunjukkan cara mereka berangkat kerja: motorbike 48.7% · car 21.4% · bus or train 19.6% · bicycle or walking 10.3%. Kamu menjelaskannya kepada manajermu lewat telepon. Lengkapi dengan jumlah yang dibulatkan, dalam bahasa Inggris: About one in ___ workers go by bus or train.
assessment.mdt-2: Kamu menjelaskan survei tentang pemakaian HP (angka latihan) kepada rekan kerja baru lewat video call. Susun ketiga bagian ini dalam urutan terbaik dan tulis hurufnya. A: Does that make sense so far? B: Just over a third use their phone mainly for work, and roughly one in ten hardly use it at all. C: Basically, most people in the survey spend more than five hours a day on their phone.
assessment.mdt-3: Mark, rekan kerja baru dari Australia yang tidak bisa membaca bahasa Indonesia, melihat artikel latihan ini: 'Mulai 1 Maret, truk barang beroda lebih dari empat dilarang melintas di jalan-jalan utama Jakarta Pusat pukul 06.00–22.00. Aturan ini sudah diuji coba selama enam bulan di tiga ruas jalan.' Lengkapi ringkasan untuknya dalam bahasa Inggris: From 1 March, big trucks can't use the main roads in central Jakarta between 6 in the morning and ___.
assessment.mdt-4: Sebuah artikel latihan yang panjang menjelaskan aturan baru untuk truk pengiriman di Jakarta Pusat. Catatanmu: A: The city tested the rule on three roads for six months. B: Traffic jams on those roads fell by about a fifth. C: Orders to central Jakarta that come in after 4 p.m. will usually arrive the next morning. D: Our company has to choose between night shifts and smaller vans. Bu Rina punya toko batik online di Bekasi dan mengirim paketnya lewat perusahaanmu. Ringkasan untuknya sebaiknya dimulai dengan catatan yang mana? Tulis hurufnya.
assessment.mdt-5: Kamu memimpin kelompok proyek di sebuah universitas di Bandung. Sudah sepuluh menit semua orang membicarakan sebuah drama Korea. Lengkapi kalimatmu untuk membawa mereka kembali ke tugas (dua kata, dalam bahasa Inggris): That's fun, but we're getting a bit off track. Let's ___ to the survey questions.
assessment.mdt-6: Di kelompok yang sama, Dimas paling banyak bicara dan Rina belum bicara selama dua puluh menit. Lengkapi ajakan yang sopan ini (tiga kata, dalam bahasa Inggris): Thanks, Dimas. Rina, we haven't ___ yet.
assessment.mdt-7: Sesinya sudah selesai. Catatanmu: disepakati → survei online, bukan wawancara · Rina → menulis pertanyaannya → paling lambat Jumat. Tulis kata bahasa Inggris yang hilang: So, to ___ up, we've agreed to do an online survey, and Rina is going to write the questions by Friday.
